principle_1_divert_before_you_wait.name: Divert before you wait
principle_1_divert_before_you_wait.summary: When a target rejects, the first move is another target that is believed healthy, with zero delay; back-off is only for the case where no alternative exists.
principle_1_divert_before_you_wait.tradeoff: Recovers a burst in milliseconds instead of seconds; spreads load onto targets that may themselves be near their limit, and consumes a request-quota slot per failed attempt.

principle_2_quarantine_on_evidence.name: Quarantine a target on evidence, and let it back in on a timer
principle_2_quarantine_on_evidence.summary: A target is removed from the candidate set for a fixed short period once its failures pass a threshold, with a minimum traffic volume so the rate is meaningful.
principle_2_quarantine_on_evidence.tradeoff: Stops a dead target absorbing a whole burst; a short fixed timer means a still-dead target is re-probed with real traffic, and the minimum-volume rule means a low-traffic target is never quarantined at all.

principle_3_never_have_nothing.name: Never let the candidate set go empty by accident
principle_3_never_have_nothing.summary: When every target is quarantined the router either refuses loudly with a 429 or, under an explicit configured policy, deliberately serves a known-bad target rather than failing.
principle_3_never_have_nothing.tradeoff: Turns a total outage into an explicit configured choice between refusing and trying anyway; the bypass path silently sends traffic to a target the system just declared unhealthy.

principle_4_pace_requests_ahead_tokens_b.name: Pace what you can predict; account for what you cannot
principle_4_pace_requests_ahead_tokens_b.summary: Request counts are reserved before the call because they are known in advance; token counts are charged after, because the real usage is not known until the answer exists.
principle_4_pace_requests_ahead_tokens_b.tradeoff: Correct request pacing for free; token pacing that is structurally one call behind and can overshoot on a single large request.

principle_5_budgets_filter_candidates.name: A budget is a filter on the candidate set, not a penalty on the objective
principle_5_budgets_filter_candidates.summary: An over-spent provider or tag is removed from consideration before placement rather than made more expensive in a score.
principle_5_budgets_filter_candidates.tradeoff: Makes the cap unbuyable; can empty the candidate set, which then falls through to the overload path.

principle_6_explain_in_band.name: Return the decision with the answer
principle_6_explain_in_band.summary: Which target served the call, how many attempts it took and what it cost travel back in the response itself.
principle_6_explain_in_band.tradeoff: Makes every request self-describing for debugging; leaks internal topology to the caller.

principle_7_unknown_price_is_not_free.name: Treat an unknown price as maximal, not as zero
principle_7_unknown_price_is_not_free.summary: A target missing from the price table is priced at an absurdly high rate so a cost-ranking policy sorts it last instead of preferring it.
principle_7_unknown_price_is_not_free.tradeoff: Fails safe against a cost blow-out on an unpriced target; also makes that target effectively unreachable under a price-ranking policy even when it is the right answer.
